precepts.text: The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God and no torment touches them; in the sight of the unwise they seem to die, but they are in peace, their hope full of immortality, and God proved them as gold in the furnace and received them as a burnt offering.
precepts.point: For God is your guide, and the guide of them that keep my commandments; let not your sins weigh you down. We do sin, and if we say we have no sin we deceive ourselves, but if we confess he is faithful to forgive; that is the difference between us and the Christian who teaches sin has no consequences. Let not your iniquities lift up themselves, for woe to them that are bound with their sins, covered as a field with thorns that no man can travel through, left undressed and cast into the fire. When you are bound, there is no magic scripture; you have to want to be released.
precepts.why:
The chosen are “tried as the gold in the fire”, and Wisdom gives more detail. “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Christ said we will be afflicted, so what does no torment mean? That is the lake of fire. That torment will not touch us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die: and their departure is taken for misery, And their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” Christ said, fear not them which kill the body; fear him who can kill body and soul. Man cannot touch your soul. They seem to die because the body died, but the real man, the real woman, is not dead. We keep falling for Esau's craftiness: it's all over, we're finished. It is not over. They are in peace; that is sleep, rest.

“For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality. And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. Jacob's trouble is just a little chastisement. “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us. Everybody says they believe; he will say, let that one get caught early and see what they do. He found them worthy because they confessed Christ before their tormentors.

“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” The death of the saints is as a burnt offering to the Lord. Christ gave his life, and he said if you will not take up your cross and follow him, you are not worthy of him.

precepts.text: Having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded, for God proved them and found them worthy for himself. What we suffer, God calls a little chastising; endure to the end.
precepts.point: One day is with the Lord as a thousand years, and a thousand years as one day. By that measure eighty years is under two hours to God. That is why God calls our trials a small moment.
precepts.why:
We feel what we are going through. We complain, we cry, we fast, we do what we can to make it through. But look what God calls it: “And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded”. A little chastised. We are not even yet at the point of being persecuted and put to death, and he calls this a little chastising.

That fits with 2 Peter 3:8: if one day with the Lord is as a thousand years, a whole lifetime of suffering is a little chastising, less than two hours in his eyes, and the reward that follows is eternal.

Then, “for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” The chastising is the proving. He tries us to find us worthy unto himself. So we have to endure to the end, people. We have to endure to the end, humbling ourselves under his mighty hand, and when the short moment is over, those found worthy will be greatly rewarded.

precepts.text: Once we are purged as gold in the furnace, we shall shine, judge the nations, and have dominion, so prepare the soul for the trials of the purge.
precepts.point: He will lay His vengeance upon Edom by the hand of His people Israel, and they shall do in Edom according to His anger and His fury. This is future prophecy that has not yet come to pass, for the Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger to perform righteous recompense with our own hands.

note.label: Ezekiel 25: Judgment on Ammon, Moab, Edom, and the Philistines

precepts.why:
Before Israel is the hand of the Most High's vengeance, Israel is tried. “As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering. And in the time of their visitation they shall shine, and run to and fro like sparks among the stubble.”

Sparks among the stubble: that is the fire of Jacob and the flame of Joseph kindling in the house of Esau. Once we are purged as gold in the furnace, we shall shine. “They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people, and their Lord shall reign for ever.”

This has not yet come to pass. The Most High must first change our minds to act according to His anger, and that comes through the purge. So prepare the soul for the trials of the purge; the gold has to go through the furnace before it shines.

precepts.text: They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth, for grace and mercy is to his saints.
precepts.point: Moses gave the first covenant; grace and truth are the new one. Where the law of Moses required a man's own blood for certain things, there is now a mediator.

note.label: John 1: The Word, the Witness of John, and the King of Israel

precepts.why:
“For the law was given by Moses, but grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.” Solomon shows where grace and truth are found and who they are for: “They that put their trust in him shall understand the truth: and such as be faithful in love shall abide with him: for grace and mercy is to his saints, and he hath care for his elect.”

Grace and mercy are said in the scriptures to be with his saints. They that put their trust in him understand the truth, and he has care for his elect. The grace and truth that came by Jesus Christ belong to his saints, his elect, the ones faithful in love that abide with him.

precepts.why: “For I am now ready to be offered, and the time of my departure is at hand.” This is heavy. Paul used the same words: I’m ready to be offered, and the time of my departure, the time of my death, is at hand. So that death is an offering: received as a burnt offering, the death of the saint is an offering to the Most High God.

note.label: ​ | Sabbath Evening Class: Secrets in the Lord's Prayer

precepts.why:
Look at the torment, so you understand the difference between you being beheaded, crucified, COVID-19, diabetes, affliction, and the torment. “If any man worship the beast”: any man worship the white man, “and his image, and receive his mark in his forehead”: you receive his mark, his policies, in your mind, “or in his hand”: you support it. “The same shall drink of the wine of the wrath of God”: you’re going to get judged. Let’s see what kind of judgment.

“Which is poured out without mixture into the cup of his indignation; and he shall be tormented with fire and brimstone”: tormented, the same word we just read in Wisdom of Solomon 3. “In the presence of the holy angels, and in the presence of the Lamb”: in the presence of Christ. “And the smoke of their torment ascendeth up for ever and ever”: your torment shall be forever and ever. “And they have no rest day nor night, who worship the beast and his image, and whosoever receiveth the mark of his name.” That is the torment that shall not touch the souls of the righteous.

precepts.why: Don’t fear them that kill the body, because that’s the fear we all fear; but the Lord says no, that ain’t the fear. “And fear not them which kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul”: Revelation 14 was talking about your soul. When I mentioned John the Baptist and Peter, I was talking about their body, not their soul. “But rather fear him which is able to destroy both soul and body in hell.” Hell is the lake of fire; that’s what you don’t want.

When we break it down, we always leave it at you’re being tempted by lust or money, sex, drugs, alcohol, and we leave it there. It’s deeper than that: Wisdom of Solomon brings it to the next level of understanding.

Peter and his wife got crucified upside down: I love that smell. Christ was the greatest; his offering took it all.

precepts.why: “And he killed James the brother of John with the sword.” The apostle James was killed with the sword, and the Lord said, an offering, another offering.

“Blessed and holy is he that hath part in the first resurrection”: meaning when Christ comes back. “On such the second death hath no power.” The second death is that final judgment, and it will have no power on us. That is the torment that shall not touch the souls of the righteous.

“The souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” The torment that shall not touch them is the lake of fire, that thermonuclear destruction that’s coming.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die”: about the beheading, it is talking about the mass tribulation, the beheading, the affliction we have just been reading about. “Their departure is taken for misery”: their departure from this earth is taken as misery, “And their going from us to be utter destruction”: it seems like we got totally destroyed, “but they are in peace.”

“For though they be punished in the sight of men”, kill them, afflict them, “yet is their hope full of immortality.” “And having been a little chastised”: the beheading, the affliction, the tribulation is called being a little chastised, and “they shall be greatly rewarded: for God proved them”. Because we all say we believe in the Lord, and he is going to say: prove it. Drink the cup that I drink, be baptized with the baptism I was baptized with. Prove yourselves.

“And found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” He is going to receive our death as a burnt offering. So real bad things are going to happen to those of us following the Lord, to prove us. Yes, we’re gonna catch hell.

“They shall judge the nations”: we’re going to judge the nations, “and have dominion over the people”: we’re going to rule over the people, “and their Lord shall reign for ever”: Christ the King of kings shall reign forever.

precepts.why:
See the mindset of our forefathers, how they thought. “So when he was ready to die he said thus, It is good, being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again by him.” His understanding and his faith said it is good to lose my life being put to death by men, to look for hope from God to be raised up again, knowing that Christ holds the keys of hell and death.

“As for thee, thou shalt have no resurrection to life.” As for you, Esau, you will have no resurrection to life. Those left behind will be servants until their time is fulfilled, and all the nations that took part in this will serve us. But there is a price for that: we have to be hated by nations and hated by our own, and we will receive eternal life.

“But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” Deacon Isaac said it best: when they leave this world, they mourn for us, because they are in paradise. Their leaving is sad for us, not for them; they are in a better place, and we are in the worst place to be. No torment touches them; the torment awaits us.

“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die”: in the sight of the wicked, the heathen, even our people, they seem to be killed, murdered off. “And their departure is taken for misery,” because there will be torture going on, “and their going from us to be utter destruction: but they are in peace.” They are at rest. “For though they be punished in the sight of men, yet is their hope full of immortality”: back to that builded city.

“And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded.” God calls torture and death a little chastisement. A little. “For God proved them, and found them worthy for himself. As gold in the furnace hath he tried them,” and the iron furnace is here, “and received them as a burnt offering,” because they got killed.

points: “But the souls of the righteous are in the hand of God, and there shall no torment touch them.” The torment that will not touch us is that lake of fire, that condemnation. No torment shall touch us.
“In the sight of the unwise they seemed to die”: they said let’s kill them, torture them; the wicked put us to death. “But they are in peace.”

When you go through bad times, wicked family members say if you weren’t in that cult this wouldn’t happen to you; come back to the Catholic Church, come back to the Baptist church. Anything that goes wrong, which is just a trial, they say it is because you are reading that Bible, because you are in that group.
“For though they be punished in the sight of men”, as we just read in Wisdom of Solomon 2, “yet is their hope full of immortality.” That is what no torment shall touch us means.

“And having been a little chastised”: what we go through in this world, in this life, God calls a little chastisement, even when it is death. “They shall be greatly rewarded”: if you endure through it, you shall be greatly rewarded. “For God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” God is going to prove us.

So whatever comes upon us, whether it is health, life, business, family, distress, persecution, bad things happening, take it cheerfully. Don’t worry. It is just a trial, brothers; it is just a trial, sisters.
“As gold in the furnace hath he tried them, and received them as a burnt offering.” He is going to receive our death like a burnt offering. The Lord likes that thing.

“And in the time of their visitation”, when the Lord returns, “they shall shine”: we shall shine, because we are going to have a new body, corruption putting on incorruption, mortal putting on immortality. “And run to and fro like sparks among the stubble”: we are going to have spiritual power.

“They shall judge the nations, and have dominion over the people”: we are going to rule the nations, brothers and sisters, and dominate all people on this earth. “And their Lord shall reign for ever”: Christ, the King of kings and Lord of lords, shall reign forever.

“And having been a little chastised, they shall be greatly rewarded: for God proved them, and found them worthy for himself.” The Most High considers what we go through, slavery, being put to death, prison, a little chastisement. Afterward we receive the reward, but we have to go through it. It is the only way to get what we are looking for, salvation and eternal life. We have to risk it all and believe.

It comes back to faith, and faith is tied directly to keeping the commandments. To have good understanding you must keep the laws; in keeping the laws your understanding grows and your faith grows, and you believe what you are reading. That is the only way we will endure: knowing that whatever happens to us, if we lose our lives in this time, we will be back.
